claim: The ModelState docstring says 't is the float nearest t₀ + k·Δt_frame, as the clock writes it, so a typed decimal on the frame grid matches it from an exact origin'.
why: src/model.jl:532 `_grid_time(model, k) = _instant(model.exec.clock, k * lattice.frame)` computes each frame top from its index and never accumulates. Probe line 062: after three step! calls at Δt_frame = 1//10 from origin 0//1, checkpoint(sim).state.t === 0.3 is true, while 0.1+0.1+0.1 = 0.30000000000000004. test/test_lattices.jl:662-693 checks the same thing from wall-clock origins.

claim: Simulation docstring lists only `join_timeout` under # Keywords; `chunk_size` (Model's) and the nine forwarded grid, algorithm and event keywords of the signature get prose, no bullet (lead)
why: src/sim.jl:360-362 sends the grid, algorithm and event keywords to Deployment and chunk_size to Model. Each has its own bullet there: src/deployment.jl:514-534 and src/model.jl:91. Rule 11's signature lines at sim.jl:310-319 name every forwarded keyword, and the Keywords list covers join_timeout, the one keyword this docstring owns. | The docstring documents the forwarded keywords by pointing to their owners, and the owners carry the bullets. No keyword is left uncovered.

claim: code_map names no entry for the shared knob validators _pace_value and _margin_value (run!, replay!, pace!, margin!) or the bound _t_end_frame
why: src/sim.jl:417-425 holds the helpers _pace_value, _margin_value and _t_end_frame. code_map.md:5-12 says an entry names constructs and does not promise to be exhaustive. Its sim.jl entry also leaves out other small helpers, such as _t_bound at sim.jl:404. | These are private validators that nobody could mistake for a design construct (code_rules.md:10-14). Leaving them out of the map contradicts nothing.

claim: overlay! signature carries trace, log, log_every, log_max; the docstring has no # Keywords list and says only 'the four recording keywords are init!'s' (lead)
why: src/sim.jl:949 points to init!'s keywords, and init!'s Keywords list (sim.jl:839-846) gives trace, log, log_every and log_max one bullet each. overlay! validates them identically through _check_recording (sim.jl:968). | The pointer reaches documented bullets, and the range refusal is stated at sim.jl:954-955.

claim: restore! signature carries trace, log, log_every, log_max in both forms; the docstring has no # Keywords list and says only 'the four recording keywords are init!'s' (lead)
why: src/sim.jl:1046 points to init!'s Keywords list (sim.jl:839-846). Both forms validate through _check_recording (sim.jl:1071, 1088) and accept the same four keywords with the same defaults.

claim: trim! signature carries baseline, t0, backend; the docstring has no # Keywords list and says only that they mean what they mean on the model's method (lead)
why: src/sim.jl:1117 'The keywords mean what they mean on the model's method'. trim!(model)'s Keywords list (trim.jl:548-557) gives baseline, t0 and backend one bullet each. The simulation's method passes them through to _solve_problem with the same defaults (sim.jl:1125-1134).

claim: linearize signature carries about, t0, width; the docstring has no # Keywords list, `width` appears only as a refusal (lead)
why: src/sim.jl:1149-1150 'The keywords mean what they mean on the model's method'. linearize(model)'s Keywords list (linearize.jl:256-263) carries about, t0 and width, width included. Both methods call the same _check_linearize_call (linearize.jl:291; sim.jl:1162). | width does not appear only as a refusal. It is covered through the pointer to the model's method.

claim: code_map 1274 lists '`to_time`' beside mode and live! as an item of sim.jl; to_time is a keyword of replay!, no definition in sim.jl
why: code_map.md:1274 groups D-219's two additions, to_time and live!, with mode. to_time is handled in sim.jl, in replay! (sim.jl:1371-1387). The map names keywords elsewhere too, for example 'The doors' recording keywords' and 't_end and ignore_stop_requests, the advances' keywords', so naming a keyword follows its own practice. The line does not claim to_time is a function. | At most the line's citation could add D-219. The item itself is not wrong.

claim: code_map names neither _replay_bound (the recording's cap on an advance) nor _settle_mode! (the flip to :live at the recording's last frame)
why: src/sim.jl:1585-1603 defines _replay_bound and _settle_mode!. code_map.md:5-12 does not promise to list every helper, and the entry for §12.7's input mode (code_map.md:1274) covers what they serve. Both are internal mechanics of spec rules (D-218), not deviations needing a map entry under code_rules.md:10-14.

claim: code_map names no entry for the run-body helpers _reset_accounts!, _register_tasks!, _residue!, _report_join_timeout!, _interrupt_source and _record
why: src/sim.jl:1785-1814, 1917, 1974 and 563 define the run-body helpers. They are private steps of constructs the map already names: _run_body!, the tail, the sweep, the termination record and the interrupt arms (code_map.md:1239-1300). The map is not exhaustive (code_map.md:5-12).
